questions.prompt: In most terrestrial food chains, which type of organism captures energy from sunlight and makes food?
choices: Decomposer
Producer (such as a green plant)
Top carnivore
Herbivore only

questions.prompt: What is the main process plants use to convert light energy into chemical energy stored in sugars?
choices: Respiration
Photosynthesis
Fermentation
Evaporation

questions.prompt: A rabbit eats grass. In this interaction, the rabbit is acting as a —
choices: producer
primary consumer (herbivore)
decomposer
sun

questions.prompt: Why is energy often drawn as a pyramid when moving through trophic levels?
choices: Because each level usually loses a large share of energy as heat and life processes, so less is available for the next level
Because predators are always smaller than prey
Because producers weigh the most in every ecosystem
Because decomposers sit at the top
questions.answer: Because each level usually loses a large share of energy as heat and life processes, so less is available for the next level

questions.prompt: Fungi and bacteria that break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients are called —
choices: producers
consumers
decomposers
pollinators

questions.prompt: Which pair best describes a *habitat* versus a *population*?
choices: Habitat: one organism; population: the whole biosphere
Habitat: where a species lives; population: all members of one species in an area
Habitat: only water; population: only land animals
They mean the same thing in ecology
questions.answer: Habitat: where a species lives; population: all members of one species in an area

questions.prompt: In a pond, algae are eaten by small fish, which are eaten by larger fish, which are eaten by herons. If pollution kills most of the algae, what is the most likely short-term effect?
choices: Herons immediately produce more algae
Energy and matter available to higher levels drop because the base of the food chain is weakened
Decomposers disappear completely
The sun stops providing energy to the pond
questions.answer: Energy and matter available to higher levels drop because the base of the food chain is weakened

questions.prompt: Which is an example of *competition* between organisms?
choices: Two species of birds using the same nesting sites when suitable trees are scarce
A bee visiting a flower for nectar while pollen sticks to its body
A worm breaking down fallen leaves
A plant making sugar using sunlight
questions.answer: Two species of birds using the same nesting sites when suitable trees are scarce

questions.prompt: In a food *web* (compared with a simple chain), multiple feeding links show that —
choices: each species eats only one other species
species may have more than one food source or predator, so ecosystems are interconnected
producers do not matter
energy increases at every level without limit
questions.answer: species may have more than one food source or predator, so ecosystems are interconnected

questions.prompt: Which change is most clearly an *adaptation* shaped by natural selection over generations?
choices: A bear learning to open a cooler at a campsite
A fox having thick fur in a cold-climate population where that trait improves survival and reproduction
A tree losing leaves in autumn because of shorter daylight today
A person wearing a coat when it is cold
questions.answer: A fox having thick fur in a cold-climate population where that trait improves survival and reproduction
